featured_videos.title: Quitting Carnivore: This Diarrhea is Horrible
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: Quitting Carnivore: This Diarrhea is Horrible
featured_videos.commentary:
The comments here are hitting different. One person's dealing with their husband in hospice and using these videos as an escape, while others are troubleshooting digestive issues and genuinely trying to help the brother stick it out. That's the real carnivore community right there, not just the wins but the messy middle where people are actually figuring it out.

Diarrhea is one of those topics that separates the "I'm fine" people from the ones actually struggling. The fat-cutting advice keeps popping up, and there's something to it, but like that California comment points out, it's not always that simple. Nervous systems, electrolytes, previous meds, individual tolerance, bile production, the whole picture matters. If your brother's considering quitting because of this, the answer probably isn't "just eat less fat" it's figuring out what his specific body needs. Some people nail carnivore immediately, some need tweaks, some need months. All of it's valid.

featured_videos.title: 6 Years Later | Is Keto Working?
featured_videos.creator: Keto Upgrade
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here nail what this video is really about, and it's worth saying out loud: keto isn't a failure just because the scale moved. Alicia's honest about gaining back some weight after six years and a pregnancy, and instead of treating that like a moral collapse, her community's response shows what actually matters. how she feels, her energy, her recipes, the inflammation gone, the food noise silenced. That's the real win. Weight loss plateaus and post-pregnancy gains are totally normal, especially when hormones shift, and it doesn't erase the metabolic improvements that stick around. If you've been on keto or carnivore long-term and felt that imposter syndrome creeping in, this is a good reminder that the scale is just one metric. Some people find that adding deliberate movement or looking at what's triggering cravings (like those blood sugar-spiking keto products someone mentioned) helps break through stalls, but the foundation. how you feel, your health markers, your relationship with food. that's what makes this worth doing for years, not weeks.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Doctor Destroys Big Pharma In ONE Video!
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Eric Westman - Adapt Your Life
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Doctor Destroys Big Pharma In ONE Video!
featured_videos.commentary: Here's what's wild: the community's not just nodding along anymore, they're getting angry. One commenter dropped "we are not made of carbohydrates" like it's the mic drop we've all been waiting for, and honestly, they're onto something that Big Pharma spent billions trying to avoid. The real frustration isn't about Westman being right (everyone knows he is at this point), it's that people are realizing they spent years. sometimes decades. taking pills for a problem that whole foods could've solved. What gets me is the person paying $300-400 a month for Ozempic while still struggling to lose weight. That's not healthcare. That's a subscription model pretending to be medicine, and the carnivore community's finally calling it out loud.

featured_videos.title: Why I Switched to Carnivore at 70
featured_videos.creator: Vicki's Retirement Journey
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why I Switched to Carnivore at 70
featured_videos.commentary: What strikes me most about these comments is how consistent the story is. People in their 70s aren't seeing carnivore as some trendy experiment, they're describing it as the thing that finally *worked* after decades of declining health. One commenter went from "15 years of declining health and energy" to feeling terrific again, and that's not an outlier here, that's the pattern. The cholesterol anxiety keeps coming up though, and I get why. Your doctor mentions high LDL and suddenly you're second-guessing yourself. We actually covered this in detail in our cholesterol section, but the short version is that the 73-year-old who's lost 80 pounds, fixed his digestion, eliminated his back and hip pain, and sleeps better has living proof carnivore works for *him*. That's the data that matters most at 70, not a number on a lab sheet divorced from how you actually feel. What these folks are really saying is simple: stop overthinking it and give it time. The weight comes off, the inflammation quiets down, and the aches that you thought were just part of getting old actually go away. That's not marketing. That's just people whose lives got visibly better.

featured_videos.title: Project 20: Losing the Regain | Back to the Basics, Meal Prep & Low Carb Eating
featured_videos.creator: DeeDee.Monroe
featured_videos.editorial_title: Project 20: Losing the Regain | Back to the Basics, Meal Prep & Low Carb Eating
featured_videos.commentary: DeeDee's framing here is exactly what works: "back to basics" isn't sexy, but it's honest. The regain hits different after you've already proven you can lose it, and the comment about perimenopause being "real" landed because it is. That's our core audience's reality. Weight loss after 40 isn't about finding a new hack, it's about meal prep discipline and staying consistent with what you know works. The phased approach someone mentioned (7 pounds at a time to 150, then reassess) is smart strategy too. It's less daunting than "lose 20 again," and psychologically it gives you real wins to celebrate along the way.

featured_videos.title: I Couldn't Find the Perfect Carnivore Bun....So I Created My Own
featured_videos.creator: Eat Like It's 1965
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Couldn't Find the Perfect Carnivore Bun....So I Created My Own
featured_videos.commentary: The community reaction here tells you something important: people aren't just looking for a workaround, they're hungry for real food that tastes like food. Notice nobody's asking for "optimal macros" or "bioavailability." They want a bun that doesn't taste like chemistry, and the fact that it took dozens of test batches to get there says something about how many half-baked carnivore products are floating around. This is the opposite of that approach, and the comments show people actually making these instead of just bookmarking and forgetting. If you've been stuck eating dry meat patties because every bread alternative tasted like cardboard, this hits different.
